one_month_reasoning: No company earnings in the window: Q3-2026 results are expected Nov 9-18 (MarketBeat estimate), after Oct 31, and Bitdeer has moved its operating updates from monthly to quarterly, so there is no October production release. In-window drivers are exogenous: the ~Oct 3 difficulty adjustment (forecast flat, -0.7% to +0.5%), bitcoin price (BTC ~$83.5k on 10/1 after a rally from ~$58k in June; hashprice ~$39/PH/day), the late-October FOMC, and possible company news such as Tydal project financing (+) or ATM selling under the new $1B program (-). The stock fell from $12.97 (9/17) to $10.64 after a 15% pop on the AI-capacity update, so there is no strong momentum signal. I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred slightly below spot (median ~$10.55, to reflect ATM selling) with monthly sigma ~0.29, a bit below 108%/3.5 because no scheduled company event falls in the window.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$5 (market cap ~$1.4B, EV ~$2.9B) the equity would be valued below the Tydal NPV plus a minimal mining value net of debt. Trading there would most likely mean something fundamental went wrong: the Tydal tenant's credit backstop failed, a financing or refinancing squeeze (BIT Group loans $491M current, converts ~$1.2B face) forced deeply dilutive equity, or BTC/hashprice collapsed to unprofitable levels. That is a different situation from ordinary 100%-vol noise.

reasoning: Facts: Aug-2026 self-mining 79.9 EH/s and 1,310 BTC/month; Q2 revenue $229M, adj. EBITDA $31M, net loss $92M; borrowings $1.84B and cash $457M at 6/30; 272M shares plus ATM. Alternative-lane signals: (1) hashprice trackers (Hashrate Index, oneminers) show hashprice up ~43% from July's record low to ~$39/PH/day, with difficulty still ~15% below its Oct-2025 peak, so Q3/Q4 mining cash flow should improve sharply versus Q2. Sell-side Q2-anchored models may lag this, though the stock has fallen anyway. (2) Prediction markets (Polymarket ~31%, Kalshi ~34% for BTC >=$100k in 2026; Aug Polymarket 85% for touching $80k) imply a roughly flat BTC central case, not a melt-up. (3) Bitdeer's careers board: 251 open roles, ~48% AI-cloud/GPU and ~10% chip design versus ~3% mining, which confirms real spending on the HPC pivot and a rising cost base. (4) CoinShares puts BTDR at 2.9x EV/NTM sales, the cheapest covered miner, with all-in cost of $89.7k/BTC in Q2 (cash $61k), above the then-BTC price. Independent research gives EV/MW of $15-16M for contracted peers (WULF/CIFR) and <$3M/MW for unleased capacity. (5) Substack bulls ($16-20 base) assume pipeline conversion. My explicit DCF of contracted cash flows gives under $1/share because corporate overhead (~$2.1B PV) and post-halving mining offset Tydal (~$1.9B NPV), so the current price already includes substantial option value on more HPC leases and BTC. Segment multiples ($11.6) and SOTP with a pipeline option ($13.8) frame the base. Blended fair value is ~$9.8, slightly below the $10.64 spot and well below the $22-24 consensus. Distribution: an equal blend of a three-scenario lognormal mixture (bear $4.8/30%, base $11/45%, bull $23/25%; mean ~$13) and a single lognormal (median $10, sigma 0.95, near realized vol of 108%), giving P(>=spot) ~0.49 with a fat right tail.
